messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: HIGH - ingress-prod eastus-a 5xx spike — severity: P1 — paging sam (oncall). Creating thread 2469004321

sam (oncall): On it. I'm seeing a 5xx surge hitting envoy in eastus-a. 5xx rate ~14% over the last 5m, latency slightly increased. Starting triage — checking LB and envoy logs.

maria: NLB console shows target health flapping in eastus-a, target count dropping from 30 -> 10 rapidly. Also seeing a handful of route propagation errors in the AZ control plane.

alex: Envoy upstream logs show a lot of "upstream reset" / ECONNRESET to backend pods. Pattern looks like the NLB is closing connections mid-stream.

jordan: Customer impact: a subset of API traffic to east region is getting 500s. CS has started notifying affected customers; AcmeCorp reported degraded API sessions.

sam (oncall): Mitigation plan: move traffic away from eastus-a while we stabilize. Maria, can you start a weighted DNS shift (Route53) to move ~20-30% to eastus-b, then monitor?

maria: Starting weighted update now — adding 30% to eastus-b, reducing eastus-a. TTL is low (30s) so propagation should be quick. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

cloud-support-bot: AWS Support case opened: 1234567891. Initial note: "NLB target health checks failing due to route table propagation delays in AZ eastus-a." Support engaged with network team.

alex: Short-term workarounds: 1) disable connection_reuse on envoy upstreams (needs config & deploy), 2) increase target group deregistration delay to allow in-flight connections to finish, 3) re-register targets to force healthy-checks. Which do we want first?

sam (oncall): Do quick host-level fix first: whitelist AWS healthcheck CIDR on affected nodes and restart kube-proxy on flapping nodes. Maria, can you patch iptables?

maria: Applied iptables accept for AWS healthcheck CIDR on 3 affected nodes and restarted kube-proxy. Verifying healthcheck locally: ```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\\n" http://localhost:8080/health
``` Returned: "200 0.012" on the patched nodes.

priya: Any immediate improvement in 5xx after the patch?

sam (oncall): Trending down — 5xx dropped to ~6% from 14% in the last 6 minutes. Still above threshold but improving.

jordan: CS: AcmeCorp still reports partial errors. Recommend routing their traffic fully to eastus-b until stable. Can we do that?

maria: I can push a per-customer routing rule in edge config for AcmeCorp to force eastus-b. Performing now with low TTL.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook step #4: If NLB healthchecks fluctuate, re-register targets to force re-evaluation. Example command: ```bash
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=i-0123456789
```

alex: I'm going to do a controlled rolling restart of envoy pods to break any stuck connections — starting with 10% subset. ```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/envoy-ingress -n prod --selector=canary=small
```

sam (oncall): Rolling restart in progress (10% batch). Observing connection reset errors drop on those pods. Good sign.

cloud-support-bot: AWS update: "We see delayed propagation of route attachments in eastus-a due to a control plane backlog. Engineering is mitigating; estimated 20-30 minutes for full stabilization."

jordan: Drafting customer message: "We're routing affected requests to a healthy region and engineering is working with the cloud provider to resolve a regional routing propagation issue. Expect reduced errors within 30 minutes." Please review before send.

priya: We should preserve session affinity for AcmeCorp when we route them to eastus-b. Can we enable header-based fallback?

alex: Added a dynamic header-rewrite rule to envoy to preserve sticky cookie during failover. Verified with a test session — cookie persists and traffic flows to eastus-b.

sam (oncall): Metrics check: 5xx now ~1.2% (near baseline). Rolling restarts complete, iptables and re-registration applied, weighted DNS at 50/50 for now.

maria: I'll keep Route53 weight at 60% eastus-b / 40% eastus-a for additional safety, TTL 30s. AWS case 1234567891 is still open and linked to the incident.

cloud-support-bot: AWS case 1234567891 updated: "Control plane backlog being cleared; route propagation now successful in eastus-a."

sam (oncall): Handing monitoring & watch to night on-call Maria in 30 minutes. Maria, escalate if 5xx > 5% or if target flapping resumes.

maria: Acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and keep weighted DNS skewed toward eastus-b until support confirms sustained stabilization.

jordan: Post-incident: scheduling a P1 postmortem and stakeholder review tomorrow 10:00 AM PT. Action items: add cross-AZ healthcheck redundancy, evaluate ALB for certain workloads, improve per-customer failover playbook.

priya: :thumbsup: Nice mitigation loop. Also add an action to test NLB healthcheck CIDR reachability and automate iptables/healthcheck rules in ASG at scale.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — please file P1 postmortem including timeline, impact numbers, and follow-ups. This thread will be locked for updates in 2 hours.
